title: Example compose: storage endpoint, credentials and bucket must be set in sync across services
answers: mlflow artifacts example cannot upload artifacts to S3 storage endpoint
docker compose example access denied or wrong endpoint for artifact store
change RustFS or MinIO credentials in mlflow_artifacts example
body:
Invariant: the storage service hostname, credentials and bucket name are repeated across services in examples/mlflow_artifacts/docker-compose.yml and must match.
- Hostname: `storage` is used in RUSTFS_SERVER_DOMAINS, in create-bucket's `--endpoint-url=http://storage:9000`, and in the tracking service's MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL.
- Credentials: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY/RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY on `storage` must equal AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY on `create-bucket` and the tracking service; the README login (`user`/`password`) must match too.
- Bucket: `bucket` is hardcoded in the create-bucket entrypoint; any rename must update it and the example client.
Skipping one breaks the artifact upload path silently or with auth errors.
Constraints: applies to this example only; the production-style setup does not use these values.
applies: Editing examples/mlflow_artifacts compose files or README login/endpoint text.
says: Artifact uploads fail with authentication errors in the sample container setup.
The sample tracking server cannot connect to the local object storage endpoint.
Login credentials listed in the example documentation do not match the container configuration.
Changing the example bucket name causes artifact saving to fail silently.
Synchronize storage credentials and endpoints across all services in the example environment.
search: Storage service hostnames, credentials, and bucket names must be synchronized across services in examples/mlflow_artifacts/docker-compose.yml and examples/mlflow_artifacts/README.md. The storage hostname must match in RUSTFS_SERVER_DOMAINS, create-bucket's endpoint URL, and MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL. Storage keys RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY and RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY must equal AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and the documentation login credentials user and password. Renaming the hardcoded bucket in the create-bucket entrypoint requires updating the example client as well, applying strictly to this example rather than production configurations.
